A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
urinary incontinence is common in older adults with diabetes, but is more common in those who have mobility and cognitive impairments.

frail elderly patients with diabetes are more likely to be incontinent than their non-frail counterparts and that incontinence is more common in patients who have difficulty ambulating and transferring independently and who are on insulin.

The main takeaway from our work is that

urinary incontinence is a significant problem among frail older adults living in the community with diabetes mellitus and that clinicians need to be vigilant about assessing and treating urinary incontinence as part of routine care for these patients.
